added.name: Section 71: Preaching in answer to Ezra Booth’s letters
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 71. Dated December 1, 1831, at Hiram. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon are to pause the Bible revision and preach, in response to Ezra Booth’s letters. Labels such as hostile or apostate belong to the Church’s account; they are not a neutral characterization of all criticism. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 72: Newel K. Whitney as bishop
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 72. Dated December 4, 1831, at Kirtland. Three revelations: first Newel K. Whitney is appointed bishop, then his duties are given, then certificates for those gathering. Whitney is to receive the accounts of his region; the bishop in Zion receives reports and certificates; three elders or the bishop certify travelers. Whitney is not substituted for Edward Partridge, the bishop in Missouri: the offices are regional. See also: “Whitney appointed bishop”, “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Bishops and the bishop’s agent”.

added.name: Section 73: The Bible revision resumed
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 73. Dated January 10, 1832, at Hiram. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon are to resume the Bible revision alongside limited preaching. No completion date is inferred from the command to finish it. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 74: On 1 Corinthians 7:14
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 74. Dated 1830 in Wayne County, New York; the current heading places it earlier than the surrounding 1832 sections. An interpretation of 1 Corinthians 7:14: children, marriage and circumcision. It is not new historical evidence about Paul. See also: “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 75: Missionaries appointed at Amherst
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 75. Dated January 25, 1832, at Amherst, Ohio, where a conference sustains and ordains Joseph Smith President of the High Priesthood; two revelations, verses 1–22 and 23–36, appoint missionaries and provide for their families. Pairs with a direction: William E. McLellin and Luke S. Johnson, south (revoking the earlier eastern assignment); Orson Hyde and Samuel H. Smith, east; Lyman E. Johnson and Orson Pratt, east; Asa Dodds and Calves Wilson, west; Major N. Ashley and Burr Riggs, south. Pairs with no direction given: Simeon Carter and Emer Harris; Ezra Thayre and Thomas B. Marsh; Hyrum Smith and Reynolds Cahoon; Daniel Stanton and Seymour Brunson; Sylvester Smith and Gideon Carter; Ruggles Eames and Stephen Burnett; Micah B. Welton and Eden Smith. Conditions of family support govern the departures. The two revelations are kept separate, directions are not turned into invented endpoints, and the assignments are instructions, not completed itineraries. See also: “Amherst, Ohio”, “Missionary assignments revised”, “Calls to preach”, “Family care, education and the poor”, “Revised companion assignments”, “Mission companions in section 75”.

added.name: Section 76: The vision of the glories
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 76. Dated February 16, 1832, at Hiram. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon report a vision received while revising John 5:29: the celestial, terrestrial and telestial glories and redemption. The realms of the vision are nonspatial theological entries, not planets or sites in Ohio. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “A shared vision of kingdoms of glory”, “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon: joint vision witnesses”.

added.name: Section 77: Questions on the book of Revelation
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 77. Dated about March 1832 at Hiram. Questions and answers interpreting the book of Revelation: symbolic creatures, seals, the 144,000 and two prophets. The interpretation assigns the seals to thousand-year periods, identifies the 144,000 as high priests and the two prophets as future Jewish prophets in Jerusalem, and describes John’s gathering mission. The text’s temporal scheme for the earth is not a geological age calculation or a dated forecast. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”.

added.name: Section 78: A firm for Zion and the poor
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 78. Dated March 1, 1832, at Kirtland. Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon and Newel K. Whitney are directed toward Missouri to organize a mercantile and publishing firm, the United Firm, for Zion and the poor, and are to confer in Zion; Michael is placed under the Holy One. The heading distinguishes the United Firm of 1832–34 from the later edited wording of “order” and storehouse: the 1832 institution is not the later United Orders, and no intermediate stops on the journey are inferred. See also: “Independence as Zion’s center place”, “The United Firm”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Members of the United Firm”.

added.name: Section 79: Jared Carter called
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 79. Dated March 12, 1832, at Hiram. Jared Carter is called on a mission; the body of the section names the eastern countries. A call is not a completed itinerary. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Missionary assignments revised”, “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 80: Stephen Burnett and Eden Smith paired
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 80. Dated March 7, 1832, at Hiram. Stephen Burnett and Eden Smith are paired, with the destination left to their choice; for this commission the pairing replaces their separate section 75 companions. The unknown destination stays unknown and is not inferred from the Ohio setting. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Missionary assignments revised”, “Calls to preach”, “Revised companion assignments”.

added.name: Section 81: A counselor in the Presidency
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 81. Dated March 15, 1832, at Hiram, with a replacement appointment on March 18, 1833. Jesse Gause originally received this appointment as counselor; Frederick G. Williams later replaced him; the formation of the Presidency. Williams is not shown receiving the appointment in March 1832, and the editorial substitution of his name in the current text stays visible. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Presidency counselor changed”, “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Jesse Gause and Frederick G. Williams”.

added.name: Section 82: The United Firm covenant
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 82. Dated April 26, 1832, at Independence. A council sustains Joseph Smith; governance of the United Firm and responsibility to one’s neighbor. Named in the covenant: Edward Partridge, Newel K. Whitney, Algernon Sidney Gilbert, Sidney Rigdon, Joseph Smith, John Whitmer, Oliver Cowdery, William W. Phelps and Martin Harris; the Kirtland stake and Zion are linked economically. The firm is not the whole church or every later communal institution. See also: “Independence as Zion’s center place”, “The United Firm”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Members of the United Firm”.

added.name: Section 83: Support for wives, children, widows and orphans
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 83. Dated April 30, 1832, at Independence. Obligations of material support for wives and children, widows and orphans; the storehouse. A normative obligation, not proof that every dependent received support. See also: “Independence as Zion’s center place”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Family care, education and the poor”.

added.name: Section 84: Priesthood lineage and the expected temple
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 84. Dated September 22 and 23, 1832, at Kirtland. Priesthood lineage, the expected temple in Missouri, provision for missionaries and a warning. The priesthood line runs back from Moses to Jethro, and from Jethro through Caleb, Elihu, Jeremy and Gad to Esaias, with the Abraham and Melchizedek chain kept separate; a New Jerusalem temple is predicted in this generation; Newel K. Whitney is instructed to visit New York, Albany and Boston. The temple prophecy is not completed construction, and the lineage is not an independently verified genealogy. See also: “Independence as Zion’s center place”, “Whitney sent to warn eastern cities”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Temple instructions”, “Priesthood genealogies”, “The priesthood line in section 84”.

added.name: Section 85: A letter to William W. Phelps
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 85. Dated November 27, 1832, at Kirtland: a letter to William W. Phelps in Independence. A clerk is to record consecrations and inheritances; a warning against unauthorized action, with an unnamed “one mighty and strong” and the steadying of the ark. No modern claimant is identified with the mighty and strong figure without separate sourced attribution. See also: “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 86: The wheat and the tares
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 86. Dated December 6, 1832, at Kirtland, in the context of the Bible revision. An interpretation of the parable of the wheat and the tares and of the claimed priesthood inheritance; Babylon and the wilderness are figurative, not literal travel. The field and the harvest are symbolic, and no map site is added. See also: “Prophecy, vision and parable”.

added.name: Section 87: A prophecy of war
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 87. Dated December 25, 1832, at or near Kirtland. A prophecy naming South Carolina’s rebellion, the Northern and Southern States and Great Britain, with future war, a slave uprising and worldwide calamity, in the context of slavery. No blanket verdict of fulfillment is given: the prophecy text and the independently documented Civil War chronology stay distinct. See also: “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Section 87: a prophecy of war”.

added.name: Section 88: The Olive Leaf
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 88. Dated December 27 and 28, 1832, and January 3, 1833, at Kirtland: three dates. Cosmology, resurrection, a house of learning and the School of the Prophets, worship and the washing of feet. Its topics include the light of Christ, resurrection and the laws of kingdoms, a cosmic parable, the ordered trumpets and resurrections, and Michael’s future battle. The symbolic cosmic order is not an astronomy dataset, and this summary does not restate every passage of the long section. See also: “School of the Prophets instructed”, “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Temple instructions”.

added.name: Section 89: The Word of Wisdom
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 89. Dated February 27, 1833, at Kirtland; the heading notes Emma Smith’s concern. Counsel on tobacco, drinks and foods, with promised blessings. The initial text says it is not given by commandment; it includes an exception for sacramental wine, hot drinks, tobacco, sparing use of meat, and grains. The 1833 wording is kept distinct from later enforcement and from modern dietary or medical claims. See also: “Word of Wisdom recorded”, “Family care, education and the poor”, “The Word of Wisdom (1833)”.

added.name: Section 90: The First Presidency and household counsel
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 90. Dated March 8, 1833, at Kirtland; the heading dates the counselors’ ordination to March 18. Sidney Rigdon and Frederick G. Williams and the First Presidency; the language of preaching; counsel to named households. Vienna Jaques is to be funded to travel to Zion in Missouri and receive an inheritance; housing for the Williams family; Joseph Smith Sr. and Rigdon are to remain. The revelation date and the ordination date are not merged, and no companion or kinship is invented for Jaques. See also: “Presidency counselor changed”, “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Family care, education and the poor”.

added.name: Section 91: The Apocrypha
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 91. Dated March 9, 1833, at Kirtland. The Apocrypha in the Bible revision: discernment and the decision not to translate it. This is not a declaration that every narrative in the Apocrypha is geographically established. See also: “Bible revision, publication and records”.

added.name: Section 92: Frederick G. Williams joins the firm
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 92. Dated March 15, 1833, at Kirtland. Frederick G. Williams is admitted to the United Firm, with the obligation of active membership. No new travel or place feature. See also: “The United Firm”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Members of the United Firm”.

added.name: Section 93: Intelligence and family duties
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 93. Dated May 6, 1833, at Kirtland. Christ, intelligence and the eternal elements: John’s witness, Christ growing from grace to grace, uncreated intelligence and eternal elements. Frederick G. Williams, Sidney Rigdon, Joseph Smith and Newel K. Whitney are rebuked concerning their duties to their families; no journeys are specified. The metaphysical teaching is not particle physics or a literal map of a pre-earth life. See also: “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”, “Family care, education and the poor”.

added.name: Section 94: Plans for houses in Kirtland
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 94. Dated August 2, 1833, at Kirtland; the current date differs from an older May placement. A house for the Presidency, a printing house and inheritances; Hyrum Smith, Reynolds Cahoon and Jared Carter form the building committee. The presidency and printing houses are each to have an inner court of 55 by 65 feet on the south lots; Hyrum Smith is assigned the third lot, and Cahoon and Carter lots to the north; construction is explicitly deferred. The proposed design is not proof of construction. See also: “Kirtland building instructions”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Temple instructions”.

added.name: Section 95: The house not yet built
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 95. Dated June 1, 1833, at Kirtland. A rebuke for failing to build the house, and its purposes of worship, instruction and endowment. The temple is to have an inner court of 55 by 65 feet, with worship below and a school above: a command and a promise, not a completed building. The construction direction is not the dedication date, which belongs to section 109. See also: “Kirtland building instructions”, “Temple instructions”.

added.name: Section 96: The French farm
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 96. Dated June 4, 1833, at a conference considering the French farm near Kirtland. The bishop is to divide the inheritances; John Johnson joins the firm; support for publication. No modern parcel geometry is assigned from the farm’s name alone. See also: “The United Firm”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Temple instructions”, “Members of the United Firm”.

added.name: Section 97: A school and a temple in Zion
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 97. Dated August 2, 1833, at Kirtland, addressed to Jackson County; the heading notes the coerced agreement of July 23. Parley P. Pratt presides over a school in Missouri; a proposed temple and its instruction; Zion as the pure in heart; protection is conditional, not unconditional immunity. The document’s origin at Kirtland is not moved to its recipients’ Missouri setting, and no completed Jackson County temple is implied. See also: “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Temple instructions”, “Meanings of Zion”.

added.name: Section 98: Renouncing war
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 98. Dated August 6, 1833, at Kirtland, in the context of persecution in Missouri. Constitutional order, renouncing war, restraint and retaliation, and forgiveness: constitutional rights; conditions for forgiveness and restitution after repeated assaults and offers of peace; the ancient Nephi, Joseph, Jacob, Isaac and Abraham as exemplars. The heading’s claim of revelatory knowledge is a religious interpretation, not an independently established history of communication. See also: “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Persecution, redress and authority”.

added.name: Section 99: John Murdock and his children
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 99. Dated August 29, 1832, at Hiram; the section number is out of chronological order. John Murdock, whose wife Julia Clapp died in April 1831, is to minister eastward after his motherless children are provided for and sent to the bishop in Zion; Murdock may later seek an inheritance. The children are unnamed, and their placements are not mapped without specific sources. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Calls to preach”, “Family care, education and the poor”, “John Murdock and Julia Clapp”, “The Knight and Murdock couples”.

added.name: Section 100: At Perrysburg
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 100. Dated October 12, 1833, at Perrysburg, New York. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon are away from their families: complementary roles of spokesman and revelator. Orson Hyde and John Gould are reassured; the journey is to continue, with the onward itinerary unstated. The reassurance about the families is the text’s claim, not an independent inspection of their conditions. See also: “Perrysburg, New York”, “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 101: After the expulsion from Jackson County
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 101. Dated December 16 and 17, 1833, at Kirtland. The expulsion from Jackson County: attempted settlement in Van Buren, Lafayette and Ray counties, with the main body of refugees in Clay County (heading context); petitions for redress. The claim to Zion is retained despite the displacement; the Saints are to buy land in Jackson and the adjoining counties and to petition the judge, then the governor, then the president; the millennial transformation and the parable of the olive trees are not dated events. The parable’s olive grove is not a real battle site, and the counties are regional only, not detailed refugee tracks or modern boundaries. See also: “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Persecution, redress and authority”, “Meanings of Zion”.

added.name: Section 102: The high council organized
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 102. Dated February 17, 1834, at Kirtland, revised on the 18th and accepted on the 19th, with additions in 1835. The organization and minutes of the high council, which met at Joseph Smith’s house, with Oliver Cowdery and Orson Hyde as recorders of the original minutes; judicial procedure. Presidents: Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon and Frederick G. Williams. The twelve councilors: Joseph Smith Sr., John Smith, Joseph Coe, John Johnson, Martin Harris, John S. Carter, Jared Carter, Oliver Cowdery, Samuel H. Smith, Orson Hyde, Sylvester Smith and Luke S. Johnson; the 43 voters are a different body. The accused has advocates and the right to a rehearing. Verses 30–32 were added in 1835, so the Twelve’s appellate provision is not assigned to the original meeting. See also: “High council rules for hearing disputes”, “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Persecution, redress and authority”.

added.name: Section 103: Recruiting a relief expedition
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 103. Dated February 24, 1834, at Kirtland. Parley P. Pratt and Lyman Wight have arrived from Missouri; a relief expedition, later called Zion’s Camp, is to be organized. Recruiting targets: 500, otherwise 300, and at least 100. Recruiting companions: Joseph Smith and Parley P. Pratt; Sidney Rigdon and Lyman Wight; Hyrum Smith and Frederick G. Williams; Orson Hyde and Orson Pratt. No actual attendance count is inferred, and the conditional promise of victory is not a completed military reconquest. See also: “Zion’s Camp organized; its objective deferred”, “Calls to preach”, “Persecution, redress and authority”.

added.name: Section 104: The firm divided into stewardships
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 104. Dated April 23, 1834, at or near Kirtland. The United Firm is restructured into individual stewardships, with separate operations and treasuries in Ohio and Missouri. Stewardships: Sidney Rigdon, his residence and the tannery; Martin Harris, a lot involved in an exchange with John Johnson; Frederick G. Williams and Oliver Cowdery, the printing; John Johnson, his inheritance less reserved lots; Newel K. Whitney, houses, the store and the ashery; Joseph Smith, the temple lot of 40 by 12 rods and his father’s home. The sacred and general treasuries are separate. The April 10 decision and the April 23 direction are distinct, and the physical parcels need separate deeds before any mapping. See also: “The United Firm”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Members of the United Firm”.

added.name: Section 105: Redemption deferred at Fishing River
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 105. Dated June 22, 1834, about four miles north of Fishing River in Clay County. Zion’s Camp has reached Missouri; the redemption of Zion is deferred after the governor declines militia support; an endowment in Kirtland is anticipated. Some are to stay, and eastern families may return as directed; peace, legal redress and the purchase of land; redemption is delayed, not an accomplished conquest. The approximate distance in the text is not a coordinate, and no exact camp is plotted. See also: “Fishing River camp region”, “Zion’s Camp organized; its objective deferred”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Persecution, redress and authority”.

added.name: Section 106: Warren A. Cowdery at Freedom
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 106. Dated November 25, 1834, at Kirtland. Warren A. Cowdery, Oliver’s older brother, is to be presiding high priest over Freedom and the surrounding region, with ministry in the adjoining counties. Freedom is a textual locality; its state and coordinates require a separate place source. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “The Pratt and Cowdery brothers”.

added.name: Section 107: Priesthood organization and the line from Adam
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 107. Dated late winter or spring 1835 at Kirtland; most of verses 60–100 incorporate a revelation of November 11, 1831. Priesthood organization; the line from Adam to Noah; the assembly at Adam-ondi-Ahman; the context of the Twelve’s mission. Adam ordains Seth, Enos, Cainan, Mahalaleel, Jared, Enoch and Methuselah; Seth ordains Lamech; Methuselah ordains Noah; ordination is not parenthood. The journey to Shedolamak is unlocated. Enoch’s age of 430 at his translation differs from the chronology of Genesis 5:23–24, and both are kept. The section is not one securely dated March 28 document, and the ancient gathering is not an 1835 event. See also: “Adam-ondi-Ahman”, “Shedolamak”, “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Priesthood genealogies”, “Ordinations in section 107”.

added.name: Section 108: Lyman Sherman seeks direction
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 108. Dated December 26, 1835, at Kirtland. Lyman Sherman, a president of the Seventy, seeks direction and is told to strengthen his fellow elders. No new route or building. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”.

added.name: Section 109: The dedicatory prayer
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 109. Dated March 27, 1836, at the Kirtland Temple; the prayer was prepared the night before. Petitions for gathering and for Israel, including the return of Jerusalem and Judah and the redemption of Israel; the existing dedication entry is reused. Verse 65’s pejorative framing of Indigenous peoples is attributed to the prayer, not to the atlas. The prayer’s requests are not proof that each requested outcome occurred. See also: “Kirtland Temple: dedication and reported vision”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Temple instructions”.

added.name: Section 110: The Kirtland Temple vision
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 110. Dated April 3, 1836, at the Kirtland Temple. Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery report seeing Christ, Moses, Elias and Elijah: Moses commits keys of the gathering, Elias the dispensation of Abraham, and Elijah keys of the dispensation and of turning the hearts of fathers and children. These visionary visits are distinguished from ordinary journeys; Elias and Elijah are not collapsed into one figure, and no modern coordinates are inferred for the vision. See also: “Vision in the Kirtland Temple”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Temple instructions”, “Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery: joint Kirtland vision witnesses”.

added.name: Section 111: At Salem
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 111. Dated August 6, 1836, at Salem, Massachusetts. Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, Hyrum Smith and Oliver Cowdery investigate a claim about money and preach; the heading gives their travel from Kirtland to Salem and back, returning without the expected money. The rented lodging is unspecified, and an inquiry about the ancient inhabitants is not a treasure discovery: no recovered treasure or treasure location is invented. See also: “Salem, Massachusetts”, “The Salem investigation”.

added.name: Section 112: Thomas B. Marsh and the Twelve
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 112. Dated July 23, 1837, at Kirtland. Thomas B. Marsh, president of the Twelve, amid dissension among the leaders; a worldwide ministry. Marsh is to keep his house in Zion while ministering among the mountains and the nations; the Twelve act under the direction of the First Presidency. No completed worldwide route is given, and no claim is made that all dissent was resolved. See also: “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “The Presidency, Marsh and the Twelve (1837)”.

added.name: Section 113: Questions on Isaiah
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 113. Dated March 1838 at or near Far West. Questions on Isaiah 11 and 52: the imagery of Jesse, and a gathered Zion and priesthood. Elias Higbee asks the Isaiah 52 questions; the stem is identified as Christ, and the rod and the root are described as descendants without personal names. The unspecified prophetic servant is not given a modern personal identity here. See also: “Far West”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”.

added.name: Section 114: David W. Patten to prepare
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 114. Dated April 11, 1838, at Far West. David W. Patten is to prepare for a future mission; the offices of the unfaithful are to be given to others. The command does not show that Patten completed the 1839 mission, and his later death requires a historical source. See also: “Far West”, “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 115: Far West and its proposed temple
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 115. Dated April 26, 1838, at Far West. The name of the church; Far West as a place of refuge and gathering; a proposed temple; leadership. The proposed house is not a completed temple, and the planned cornerstone dates are kept apart from records of actual events. See also: “Far West”, “Far West temple directed”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Temple instructions”, “Meanings of Zion”.

added.name: Section 116: Spring Hill named Adam-ondi-Ahman
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 116. Dated May or June 1838 at Spring Hill, near Wight’s Ferry in Daviess County. Spring Hill is named Adam-ondi-Ahman, the setting of an anticipated gathering with Adam, the Ancient of Days. The current heading gives no exact May 19 date, and the religious identification is not independent archaeology of an ancient site. See also: “Adam-ondi-Ahman”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Meanings of Zion”.

added.name: Section 117: William Marks, Newel K. Whitney and Oliver Granger
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 117. Dated July 8, 1838, at Far West. William Marks is called from Kirtland to preside at Far West; Newel K. Whitney is directed to Adam-ondi-Ahman; Oliver Granger is to handle the Presidency’s financial obligations. Olaha Shinehah is the text’s plain where Adam dwelt. Olaha Shinehah is not split into two invented sites, no ancient archaeology is inferred from the religious identification, and Marks and Whitney are not treated as a traveling pair. See also: “Far West”, “Adam-ondi-Ahman”, “Olaha Shinehah”, “Kirtland obligations and new assignments”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Family care, education and the poor”, “Meanings of Zion”.

added.name: Section 118: Vacancies in the Twelve
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 118. Dated July 8, 1838, at Far West. The vacancies in the Twelve are filled and a mission is directed to depart from the temple site the following spring: Thomas B. Marsh is to remain to publish in Zion; John Taylor, John E. Page, Wilford Woodruff and Willard Richards are appointed to the vacancies. “Thomas” is resolved as Marsh by the current official footnote. The command to depart is not proof the journey happened, and the date of the document is distinct from any event. See also: “Far West”, “Far West temple directed”, “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Calls to preach”.

added.name: Section 119: Surplus property and tithing
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 119. Dated July 8, 1838, at Far West. Surplus property and an annual tithing on interest; the heading clarifies the historical meaning of earlier tithing. Earlier references to tithing are not flattened into a present-day accounting definition. See also: “Far West”, “Tithing and its administration instructed”, “Gathering, land and consecration”.

added.name: Section 120: A council for tithed property
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 120. Dated July 8, 1838, at Far West. A council is to dispose of tithed property: the Presidency, the bishop and his council, and the high council. No new geographic feature; the administrative concept is linked with section 119. See also: “Far West”, “Tithing and its administration instructed”, “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Gathering, land and consecration”.

added.name: Section 121: From Liberty Jail: power and persuasion
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 121. Dated March 20 and about March 22, 1839, at Liberty Jail: two epistles. Suffering, power and persuasion; the existing Liberty Jail place and the “Letters from Liberty” event are reused. The Missouri River analogy is not a journey; threats against accusers and promises of future cosmological knowledge remain the text’s attributed claims, alongside its limits on coercive authority. The whole section is not dated March 20, and unjust power is not equated with righteous priesthood. See also: “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Persecution, redress and authority”.

added.name: Section 122: From Liberty Jail: adversity
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 122. Dated about March 22, 1839, at Liberty Jail. A prison epistle on adversity and Christ’s descent: a pastoral response to suffering. The scenario of a six-year-old eldest son is part of conditional rhetoric, and no route by sea or pit is inferred. The hypothetical dangers are not all documented incidents. See also: “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Persecution, redress and authority”.

added.name: Section 123: From Liberty Jail: gathering the record of losses
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 123. Dated about March 22, 1839, at Liberty Jail. The Saints are to collect affidavits and a history of their losses, publish their grievances and seek a public hearing: property and personal losses, the names of perpetrators, publications and affidavits, to be presented to the government and the public. The mandate to collect is not a finished register of claims. See also: “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Persecution, redress and authority”.

added.name: Section 124: Nauvoo: temple, house and offices
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 124. Dated January 19, 1841, at Nauvoo, formerly Commerce. Distinct instructions for the Nauvoo temple, including proxy baptism, and for the Nauvoo House, a boarding house. A proclamation is to be written with Robert B. Thompson’s help and John C. Bennett’s labor, with Sidney Rigdon and William Law as further assistants. Nauvoo House trustees: George Miller, Lyman Wight, John Snider and Peter Haws; the president to be chosen among them is unnamed. Stock is set from $50 to $15,000; Joseph Smith Jr., Vinson Knight, Hyrum Smith, Isaac Galland, William Marks, Henry G. Sherwood, William Law, Amos Davies and Robert D. Foster are directed to subscribe, and Foster is instructed concerning building a house for Smith. Isaac Galland is to be ordained by William Marks and to go with Hyrum Smith, and a future mission of William Law with Hyrum is reserved; Law is to preach at Warsaw, Carthage, Burlington and Madison; Rigdon is to move near Smith, not east. Offices: Hyrum Smith, patriarch and seer; William Law replaces him as counselor; the Presidency of Joseph Smith with Sidney Rigdon and William Law. Brigham Young presides over the Twelve: Heber C. Kimball, Parley P. Pratt, Orson Pratt, Orson Hyde, William Smith, John Taylor, John E. Page, Wilford Woodruff, Willard Richards and George A. Smith, with the deceased David W. Patten noted; no twelfth living name is invented. High council: Samuel Bent, Henry G. Sherwood, George W. Harris, Charles C. Rich, Thomas Grover, Newel Knight, David Dort, Dunbar Wilson, Aaron Johnson (replacing the deceased Seymour Brunson), David Fullmer, Alpheus Cutler and William Huntington. High priests: Don C. Smith, president, with Amasa Lyman and Noah Packard. Elders: John A. Hicks, Samuel Williams and Jesse Baker. Seventy: Joseph Young, Josiah Butterfield, Daniel Miles, Henry Herriman, Zera Pulsipher, Levi W. Hancock and James Foster. Bishopric: Vinson Knight, Samuel H. Smith and Shadrach Roundy, Roundy “if he will receive it”; Samuel Rolfe presides over the priests. The deaths of David W. Patten, Edward Partridge, Joseph Smith Sr. and Seymour Brunson are remembered, and the oppressed builders of the Jackson County temple are excused, not shown as having completed it. Commanded appointments and construction are kept apart from their completion; ward presidents are unnamed, and household and property coordinates require historical sources. See also: “Nauvoo House”, “Nauvoo building and leadership instructions”, “Law’s regional preaching assignment”, “Offices, ordinances and discipline”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Temple instructions”, “Family care, education and the poor”, “Joseph and Hyrum Smith: brothers with distinct offices”, “Offices named in section 124”.

added.name: Section 125: The Saints in Iowa
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 125. Dated March 1841 at Nauvoo, addressed to the Saints in Iowa. Instructions for settlement and gathering, naming Zarahemla and Nashville in Iowa. Iowa’s Zarahemla is not identified with the Book of Mormon city, and the recipients’ location is not the document’s origin. See also: “Zarahemla, Iowa”, “Gathering, land and consecration”, “Meanings of Zion”.

added.name: Section 126: Brigham Young home from England
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 126. Dated July 9, 1841, at Brigham Young’s home in Nauvoo. Young has returned from a mission in England of nearly two years; care for his family and relief from travel. This is not a claim that Young never traveled again; the counsel is contextual. See also: “Calls to preach”, “Family care, education and the poor”.

added.name: Section 127: A letter on recording proxy baptisms
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 127. Dated September 1, 1842, at Nauvoo: an epistle. Joseph Smith leaves temporarily for safety; records and witnesses for proxy baptism, with an eyewitness recorder and a temple archive; the letter promises further instruction by mail. His claim of legal innocence is attributed advocacy, not a new judgment by the atlas. See also: “Proxy-baptism records instructed”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Temple instructions”, “Persecution, redress and authority”, “Proxy baptism, witnesses and records”.

added.name: Section 128: Recorders, baptism for the dead and the keys
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 128. Dated September 7, 1842, at Nauvoo: an epistle. Local and general recorders and baptism for the dead; a recapitulation of voices and keys names Cumorah, Fayette and the Susquehanna. The ancient identification of Cumorah and the exact date of each visitation remain separate evidence questions. See also: “Proxy-baptism records instructed”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Temple instructions”, “Proxy baptism, witnesses and records”.

added.name: Section 129: Distinguishing messengers
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 129. Dated February 9, 1843, at Nauvoo. Instruction distinguishing resurrected beings from spirits, with diagnostic signs; the handshake test is theological teaching, not an empirical investigative method. No supernatural beings are plotted as verified physical sightings. See also: “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”.

added.name: Section 130: Instructions at Ramus, April 1843
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 130. Dated April 2, 1843, at Ramus, Illinois. The celestial earth; the embodied Father and Son; intelligence; the timing of the Second Coming withheld. The statement about age 85 does not permit computing a certain date of return, and the cosmology is not astronomical coordinates. See also: “Ramus instructions”, “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”, “Sections 130 and 131”.

added.name: Section 131: Instructions at Ramus, May 1843
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 131. Dated May 16 and 17, 1843, at Ramus. Marriage and exaltation, assurance, and spirit as matter. Nonspatial doctrine: not a physics measurement or a universal historical claim about marriage. See also: “Ramus instructions”, “Prayer, spiritual gifts and agency”, “Sections 130 and 131”.

added.name: Section 132: Eternal and plural marriage
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 132. Recorded July 12, 1843, at Nauvoo; its principles were known earlier. Eternal marriage, plural marriage, the examples of Abraham, and instructions to Emma Smith. Verses 54 and 64 threaten destruction for refusal; verse 61 speaks of the first wife’s consent, and verse 65 of an exemption that applies when she refuses; both stay visible. The exception concerning David and Uriah, and the tension with Jacob 2:24, are attributed rather than flattened. The recording date is not the start of every practice, the difficult passages on Emma and consent are not omitted, and further historical voices are still needed. See also: “Eternal and plural marriage teachings recorded”, “Consent and command in section 132”, “Joseph Smith and Emma: spouses”.

added.name: Section 133: The appendix: gathering out of Babylon
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 133. Dated November 3, 1831, at Hiram; originally an appendix. Gathering out of Babylon; Zion and Jerusalem and a future transformed earth; a worldwide proclamation. Judah is to gather to Jerusalem and the Gentiles to Zion; a future appearance on Olivet, the ocean and the islands; the tribes of the north country and their highway are unlocated; spiritual Babylon is explicitly figurative. The section number is not chronological, and the anticipated merging of continents is not a geological reconstruction. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Prophecy, vision and parable”, “Meanings of Zion”.

added.name: Section 134: A declaration on government
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 134. Dated August 17, 1835, at an assembly in Kirtland. A declaration on government, law and conscience, adopted with the publication of the scriptures; it distinguishes religion from civil authority. It is not presented as a dictated revelation, and verse 12’s slavery-era qualification is not erased. See also: “Government declaration adopted”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Persecution, redress and authority”, “Section 134 on civil government”.

added.name: Section 135: The announcement of the deaths at Carthage
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 135. An event of June 27, 1844, at Carthage Jail, announced in the 1844 edition. Joseph Smith and his brother Hyrum are killed; in the account John Taylor is wounded and Willard Richards spared; a memorial testimony. The time of about 5 p.m. and a mob of 150 to 200 are the account’s estimates, and the quotation from Ether 12 and the praise are memorial witness, not independently neutral judgments. The announcement’s estimates and rhetoric need independent corroboration before being treated as statistics, and its authorship is not assigned to Taylor alone. See also: “Deaths at Carthage”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Persecution, redress and authority”, “Joseph and Hyrum Smith: brothers with distinct offices”.

added.name: Section 136: Instructions at Winter Quarters
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 136. Dated January 14, 1847, at Winter Quarters on Omaha land. Brigham Young’s instructions for the camps: captains and support for vulnerable families. Company organizers: Ezra T. Benson and Erastus Snow; Orson Pratt and Wilford Woodruff; Amasa Lyman and George A. Smith. Spring pioneers, crops and houses for those who stay, and shared support for the poor, widows, orphans and the families of men in the army. The verses do not name Salt Lake as the destination. The section does not show the Omaha people’s consent or every wagon’s exact route, and the modern anchor is the visitor center. See also: “Westward companies prepare mutual support”, “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Family care, education and the poor”, “Organizers of the westward companies”.

added.name: Section 137: A vision including Alvin
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 137. Dated January 21, 1836, at the Kirtland Temple. A vision including Alvin Smith: salvation beyond earthly knowledge, and children. Adam, Abraham, Joseph’s parents and Alvin are shown; those who would have received the gospel and children below the age of accountability are promised salvation. The vision includes parents then living; it is not a notice of deaths. It comes before section 109 in time, and the vision has no celestial or earthly coordinate. See also: “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Joseph Smith and his brother Alvin”.

added.name: Section 138: The vision of the redemption of the dead
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 138. A vision of October 3, 1918, at Salt Lake City, accepted by Church leaders on October 31. Joseph F. Smith’s vision of Christ and his messengers among the dead, with Adam and Eve and the prophets; the existing vision cards are reused. Pontus, Galatia and Cappadocia come from Peter’s epistle; Christ commissions messengers rather than personally visiting the wicked; Eve and her daughters, Abel, Seth, Shem, the patriarchs and prophets and later leaders appear; Hyrum Smith is explicitly Joseph F. Smith’s father. October 31 is not called a general-conference canonization, and no exact room is assigned without a source. See also: “Bible revision, publication and records”, “Section 138: messengers to the dead”, “Joseph F. Smith, son of Hyrum”.

added.name: Official Declaration 1: The Manifesto
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Official Declaration 1. Wilford Woodruff’s statement, the Manifesto, is dated September 24, 1890, and was accepted on October 6, 1890, at a conference in Salt Lake City on Lorenzo Snow’s motion; the existing “Manifesto accepted” event is reused. The appended material includes an account of the Endowment House demolition and excerpts of addresses at Logan in 1891 and at the Salt Lake Temple in 1893, labelled as separate settings. The statement’s denials are read with the Church’s later acknowledgment of plural marriages after 1890; it was not an instantaneous end of all unions. See also: “Manifesto issued and explained”, “The Official Declarations: announcement and acceptance”, “Consent and command in section 132”, “Signatories and the motion to accept”.

added.name: Official Declaration 2: The priesthood restriction removed
added.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Official Declaration 2. A temple confirmation reported on June 1, 1978, a letter dated June 8 and acceptance on September 30: the racial restriction on priesthood is removed. Spencer W. Kimball, N. Eldon Tanner and Marion G. Romney signed the letter; Tanner presented it to the conference; Kimball is the reported recipient of the revelation, confirmed on June 1 per the heading. The anonymous editorial heading is not attributed to these men. This was not the first baptism of Black members or an ordination of women to the priesthood, and the heading’s acknowledgment that the origins are unclear is not a statement that no harm was done. See also: “The Official Declarations: announcement and acceptance”, “Signatories and the motion to accept”.

before.name: Section 36: Edward Partridge called
before.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 36. Dated December 9, 1830, near Fayette. Edward Partridge is called and Sidney Rigdon lays hands on him; instruction on priesthood and mission. No travel path is added, and the wording of ordination or confirmation follows the text rather than an inferred office. See also: “Calls to preach”.

after.name: Section 36: Edward Partridge called
after.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 36. Dated December 9, 1830, near Fayette. Edward Partridge is called to preach; verse 2 promises that the Lord will lay his hand on him through Sidney Rigdon and that he will receive the Holy Ghost. The section gives priesthood and mission instructions. No travel path is added, and the wording of ordination or confirmation follows the text rather than an inferred office. See also: “Calls to preach”.

before.name: Section 52: Companions sent to Missouri
before.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 52. Dated June 6, 1831, at a conference in Kirtland, directing a gathering in Missouri. Pairs: Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon; Lyman Wight and John Corrill; John Murdock and Hyrum Smith, by way of Detroit; Thomas B. Marsh and Ezra Thayre; Isaac Morley and Ezra Booth; Edward Partridge and Martin Harris to join Smith; David Whitmer and Harvey Whitlock; the Pratt brothers; Solomon Hancock and Simeon Carter; Edson Fuller and Jacob Scott; Levi Hancock and Zebedee Coltrin; Reynolds Cahoon and Samuel H. Smith; Wheeler Baldwin and William Carter; Newel Knight and Selah J. Griffin. Joseph Wakefield and Solomon Humphrey are assigned east; Heman Basset is replaced by Simonds Ryder; Jared Carter and George James are ordained priests. The pairs and destinations are instructions, not completed itineraries, and section 56 revises the pairings. See also: “Missionary assignments revised”, “Calls to preach”, “Mission companions in section 52”.

after.name: Section 52: Companions sent to Missouri
after.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 52. Dated June 6, 1831, at a conference in Kirtland, directing a gathering in Missouri. Assignments include: Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon; Lyman Wight and John Corrill; John Murdock and Hyrum Smith, by way of Detroit; Thomas B. Marsh and Ezra Thayre; Isaac Morley and Ezra Booth; Edward Partridge and Martin Harris to travel with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon as one party; David Whitmer and Harvey Whitlock; the Pratt brothers; Solomon Hancock and Simeon Carter; Edson Fuller and Jacob Scott; Levi Hancock and Zebedee Coltrin; Reynolds Cahoon and Samuel H. Smith; Wheeler Baldwin and William Carter; Newel Knight and Selah J. Griffin. Joseph Wakefield and Solomon Humphrey are assigned east; Heman Basset is replaced by Simonds Ryder; Jared Carter and George James are ordained priests. The pairs and destinations are instructions, not completed itineraries, and section 56 revises the pairings. See also: “Missionary assignments revised”, “Calls to preach”, “Mission companions in section 52”.

before.name: Section 54: The Colesville migrants go on
before.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 54. Dated June 10, 1831, at Kirtland, addressed to the community at Thompson. Newel Knight leads the Colesville migrants after the agreement for Leman Copley’s farm breaks down, and they leave for Missouri. This records a failed settlement arrangement, not an assumed permanent inheritance at Thompson. See also: “Calls to preach”.

after.name: Section 54: The Colesville migrants directed onward
after.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 54. Dated June 10, 1831, at Kirtland, addressed to the community at Thompson. The heading identifies Newel Knight as leader of the community at Thompson after Leman Copley’s farm agreement broke down. The revelation commands that community to leave the farm and journey to Missouri; it does not itself record their completed departure or arrival. This records a failed settlement arrangement, not an assumed permanent inheritance at Thompson. See also: “Calls to preach”.

before.name: Section 60: Directions for the return east
before.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 60. Dated August 8, 1831, at Independence. The returning elders are directed to St. Louis; Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon and Oliver Cowdery are to go on to Cincinnati; the others preach on their way home in pairs. Edward Partridge supplies travel money, to be repaid as they are able. Permission for transport is not a confirmed route. See also: “Independence as Zion’s center place”, “Calls to preach”, “Gathering, land and consecration”.

after.name: Section 60: Directions for the return east
after.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 60. Dated August 8, 1831, at Independence. The returning elders are directed to St. Louis; Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon and Oliver Cowdery are to go on to Cincinnati; the others are to preach on their way home in pairs. Edward Partridge is directed to supply travel money, to be repaid as they are able. Permission for transport is not a confirmed route. See also: “Independence as Zion’s center place”, “Calls to preach”, “Gathering, land and consecration”.

before.name: Section 70: Stewards of the revelations
before.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 70. Dated November 12, 1831, at Hiram. Stewards of publication are appointed; spiritual labor and temporal equality. Stewardship is not merged with ownership of every manuscript. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.

after.name: Section 70: Stewards of the revelations
after.desc: Doctrine and Covenants — Section 70. Dated November 12, 1831, at Hiram. Stewards of publication are appointed; spiritual labor and temporal equality. Section 70:1–5 names Joseph Smith Jr., Martin Harris, Oliver Cowdery, John Whitmer, Sidney Rigdon and William W. Phelps as stewards of the revelations and their publication. Stewardship is not merged with ownership of every manuscript. See also: “Hiram, Ohio”, “Revelation publication assigned”, “Bible revision, publication and records”.
